title: Love as Building, Not Feeling
author: Chris Martin
source: The Ways of a Gentleman, February 25, 2026
summary: Martin argues against contemporary cultural celebration of independence, contending that marriage and family are the natural destination of honorable love. He frames courtship not as entertainment but as preparation for lifelong commitment. Men who choose responsibility discover fulfillment. Martin explains that love is meant to move beyond perpetual romance into permanence, and family structure provides meaning that casual relationships cannot. The piece challenges masculine autonomy narratives by demonstrating that bound commitment to wife and children produces deeper satisfaction than extended singleness or perpetual dating.
points: Love moves from romance toward permanence; marriage is natural destination of honorable love
Courtship is preparation, not entertainment; affection has meaningful consequences
Men who choose responsibility discover fulfillment that independence culture misses
Marriage and family not relics of past but natural outcome of mature love
Commitment binds men to purpose; permanence produces meaning single life cannot
quotes: Love is not meant to remain suspended in perpetual romance or an endless cycle of casual relationships.
Courtship was not entertainment; it was preparation for a lifelong relationship.
For generations, men instinctively understood this concept.
In a culture that seems to celebrate independence above everything else, the idea of binding oneself permanently to another person might seem odd to some men.

Yet time and time again, the men who choose responsibility discover fulfillment in life. Marriage and family are not relics of a bygone era.” Archived from The Ways of a Gentleman on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
